what: Story presets: one fully timed story inside a format, brand-free, filled by the writing chain with the brand's own research, dials and house rules. First shelf: the 47 Higgsfield Drama Ads cards, as our structured version (the capture stays data, workspace rule 8).

checks.ask: Does the first frame show the conflict between two characters, readable in 3 seconds with no context (no scenery first, no document or screen to read)?
Does a stranger know the kind of situation in 5 seconds and, within 10, who each character is to the others, in the plain words of their world?
Is every conflict shown on screen, with at most one world rule the viewer must learn?
Does no line carry more than two facts, no villain confess for the viewer, and no character explain their own feelings?
Does every turn in the hero's favour, the product's arrival included, come from a deliberate act (theirs or the mentor's), and was everything the ending turns on planted before it?
Do the turn and the ending read with the sound off and no readable text?
Does the piece end on a concrete, visible action that answers the hook?
Can every action happen by the world's own physics and be shown by the video model: at most two bodily contacts and one change of state per 30 seconds, each across a cut?
No brand but ours, no real people or known characters, nothing sexualised, everyone clothed, a child only in an everyday scene?
